title: Shaded seating at the Nirolhu Magu bus stops
locationText: Bus stops along Nirolhu Magu between the ferry terminal and Central Park
whatChanges: Replace the open-frame bus shelters with shaded structures using the same design language as the promenade pavilions. Add a bench, a bin, and a small planter per stop. Six stops in total.
benefit: Waiting passengers stand in direct sun between 10am and 4pm. Shade would make the bus a realistic option for elderly residents and school children, and reduce the number of people waiting inside nearby shops.
impact: Minor: the shelters take the same footprint as today. Construction could be done one stop at a time so no stop is out of service for more than a week.
statusNote: SPES has invited the submitter to a design session with the mobility team on 5 October.

title: Community garden on the vacant lot behind CF-03
locationText: Vacant lot behind the planned community facility site CF-03
whatChanges: Set up raised beds, a rain-water tank and a tool shed on the lot until it is needed for construction. Plots allocated to households in the surrounding blocks by lottery, with a few beds reserved for the school.
benefit: Phase 2 has very little usable green space while blocks are still going up. A garden gives neighbours a reason to meet and gives the school a practical science space.
impact: Temporary use only; everything is movable. Needs a water connection and an agreement on who maintains it.
statusNote: Estate is checking the construction schedule for the lot.

title: Weekend night market on the east waterfront
whatChanges: Allow a licensed Friday and Saturday evening market with 30 to 40 stalls on the widened section of the promenade, with fixed power points and a waste station.
benefit: Gives home businesses a low-cost place to sell and brings evening footfall to the waterfront, which is empty after dark.
impact: Noise for the closest apartment block; would need a 11pm cut-off and a cleaning contract. Cycling lane must stay clear.
